ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diagonals $AC, BD$ of the rhombus $ABCD$ intersect at point $O$. If $AC=4, BD=6$, what is the length of $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since rhombus $ABCD$ has diagonals $AC, BD$ intersecting at point $O$, and $AC=4, BD=6$,\\
it follows that $AC\perp BD$, $AO=\frac{1}{2}AC=2$, $BO=\frac{1}{2}BD=3$,\\
In $\triangle AOB$, $AB^2=AO^2+BO^2$,\\
thus $AB=\sqrt{AO^2+BO^2}=\sqrt{2^2+3^2}=\boxed{\sqrt{13}}$.
